title: How Bras Work
summary: Josh and Chuck (with Chuck's notes that Jerry is absent) cover the history and design of the bra, from ancient Sicilian mosaics and medieval breast bags through the corset era, the 1863 patent by Luman Chapman, Mary Phelps Jacobs' backless brassiere and its 1914 patent, the World War One steel shortage, 1920s-1960s styles (Boyische Form, Maidenform, bullet bras, Rudi Gernreich's no-bra), the Wonderbra, cup and band sizing, bra fitting and Dorothy Gallagher as a fit model, Victoria's Secret, the 1968 Miss America protest 'bra burning' myth, a French study on going braless, and a listener email about bum guns.
topics: World War One steel corset shortage

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to bras
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the ghost studio and past episodes, then introduce the topic of bras, the word's uncertain origin, and the modern bra's complicated role in society. They also chat about Porsches and cars.

segments.title: Bra complexity, sports bras, and the bra industry
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how difficult bras are to design, the jog bra invented from jockstraps, a quote from Uplift on what bras must do, bra market size, and the number of styles and patterns.

segments.title: Ancient and medieval precursors
segments.summary: The hosts describe a Sicilian mosaic of athletic women in bikini-like tops, the Greek epodesmi and Latin strophium, medieval breast bags described by Honoré de Mondeville, and the 700-year-old linen bras found at Langenberg Castle in Austria.

segments.title: Corsets and the first modern bra patents
segments.summary: The hosts explain how corsets shaped the torso from the bottom up while bras suspend from the shoulders. Luman Chapman filed an 1863 patent for an over-the-shoulder design, and Hermance Cadolle created a two-piece corset-style design.

segments.title: Mary Phelps Jacobs and World War One
segments.summary: Mary Phelps Jacobs at age nineteen had a maid make a backless brassiere from handkerchiefs and ribbon; she patented it in 1914 and sold it to Warner Brothers Corset Company for $1,500. Wartime steel shortages pushed American women away from corsets toward elastic fabrics and latex.

segments.title: 1920s to 1960s bra styles and advertising
segments.summary: The hosts cover Boyische Form in the 1920s, Maidenform's 'I Dream' campaign by William and Ida Rosenthal, the bullet and torpedo bras of the 1940s and 1950s, and Rudi Gernreich's no-bra of the 1960s.

segments.title: Wonderbra, stigma, and training bras
segments.summary: The Wonderbra is discussed as a Canadian invention that reached America in the 1990s. The hosts discuss the social stigma of going braless and the psychology of training bras.
